writeup.headline: Energy Transfer rates Buy on strong growth and low absolute valuation, but a weak balance sheet keeps it at the edge.
writeup.thesis: Energy Transfer scores 65, the lowest point of the Buy band. Growth is the standout factor at 98, with TTM revenue growth of 33.3% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 78.4% year on year, as growth sped up by 46.3 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 85 because the multiples are low in absolute terms: P/S of 0.7x, P/FCF of 13.7x, EV/EBIT of 12.9x, and FCF yield 2.3 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield; there is no comparison with its own history. Holding the score back are a balance sheet score of 1, with net debt at 12.91 times FCF and cash covering only 0.01 of debt, and middling quality at 46, with a 23.6% gross margin, 10.0% operating margin and 4.9% FCF margin. Trend (65) and news (59) are moderately supportive, helped by the Vaquero Midstream deal and Mizuho's target raise with a Buy kept.
key_risks: Heavy leverage: net debt is 12.91 times FCF and cash covers only 0.01 of debt
Thin margins, with a 4.9% FCF margin leaving little cushion if volumes or prices soften
The $2.625 billion Vaquero purchase and $5.6–$5.9 billion of 2026 growth capital add spending pressure on an already stretched balance sheet
Q3 results on November 3 could disappoint after the August guidance raise
Shares are trailing the market slightly: 0.6 pp behind SPY and 1.5 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days
